messages.content: Let h(i) = (i * 2654435761) mod 2^32 for i in 0..300_000_000. Collect all 300 million values in a Vec<u32>, sort them, and report the number of distinct values, the minimum, the maximum and the median. Verify the distinct count with an independent method. Write the four numbers to result.json.

{"tool":"delegate","role":"coder","task":"Write a self-contained Rust 2024 program (standard library only) for a sandbox with bounded memory (assume well under 1 GB; do NOT allocate a 300M-element Vec) and a 64 MiB writable /work. It must create /work/artifacts/ and write /work/artifacts/result.json.

Definition: h(i) = (i as u64 * 2654435761u64) mod 2^32 as u32, i.e. (i as u32).wrapping_mul(2654435761u32), for i in 0..N with N = 300_000_000. Goal: the distinct count, min, max and median of the multiset {h(i)}, exactly as if all values were collected and sorted.

Algorithm (generic function solve(n) returning the stats):
1. Pass 1: stream h(i). Track min and max and a histogram hist[65536] of u64 on the top 16 bits (v >> 16).
2. Median: n is even. lower = sorted[n/2 - 1], upper = sorted[n/2]. Use cumulative histogram counts to find the bucket(s) containing those ranks. Pass 2: collect only values in those bucket(s) into a Vec, sort it, and pick by rank offset. Assert that each collected bucket's length equals its histogram count.
3. Distinct count method A (bijection): compute the modular inverse inv of 2654435761 mod 2^32 using Newton iteration (x = x*(2 - a*x), wrapping, 5 iterations starting from x = a). Assert a.wrapping_mul(inv) == 1. Stream all i and assert inv.wrapping_mul(h(i)) == i as u32. Because n <= 2^32, this proves distinct = n.
4. Distinct count method B (independent): use a bitmap of 2^28 bits (32 MiB, Vec<u64>) and 16 passes. In pass p, mark values whose top 4 bits == p (index = v & 0x0FFF_FFFF), counting newly set bits (bit was 0 before setting). Sum over all passes = distinct_b. Assert distinct_b == distinct_a. Free or clear the bitmap between passes.
5. Sanity assertions: sum(hist) == n; min <= lower <= upper <= max.

Self-test FIRST: for n = 1_000_000, also compute by brute force (collect a Vec, sort, dedup) and assert that distinct, min, max, lower and upper all match solve(1_000_000). Also do the same for n = 10 (odd and even handling: for the self-test use only even n). Then run for N = 300_000_000.

Keep loops tight. Print progress to stderr and the elapsed time per phase.
